senses.d: The act of paying.
ex: Payment will be made at the end of the month.

senses.d: An instance of that act; a sum of money paid in exchange for goods or services, or the transaction that conveys it.
Something of value given in return for an act; payback; recompense; reward.
ex: I humbly apologize for my behavior. Please accept this as payment for your kindness and patience.
I do hope this is a fair exchange, my story in payment for your kindness.

From Middle English payen, from Old French paiier (“pay”), from Medieval Latin pācāre (“to settle, satisfy”) from Latin pācāre (“to pacify”). In this sense, displaced native Old English ġield (“pay”) and ġieldan (“to pay”), whence Modern English yield.
From Old French peier, from Latin picāre (“to cover with pitch”).

senses.d: To give money or other compensation to in exchange for goods or services.
ex: pay cash or pay in cash, pay by credit/debit card
pay in dollars/euros, etc.

senses.d: To deposit into an account.
ex: I pay a portion of each paycheck into a savings account.

senses.d: To discharge, as a debt or other obligation, by giving or doing what is due or required.
ex: to pay compensation, to pay a fine
She offered to pay the bill.

senses.d: To be profitable; to be worth it.
ex: It didn't pay him to keep the store open any more.
Crime doesn’t pay.

senses.d: To cover, as a cost.
ex: Those investments paid for her college education.

senses.d: To yield as a benefit.
ex: to pay dividends; to pay interest
You will get paid from this investment yearly.

senses.d: To give (something else than money).
ex: to pay attention, to pay tribute, to pay a visit
not paying me a welcome

senses.d: To suffer consequences, especially justly.
ex: He paid for his fun in the sun with a terrible sunburn.

senses.d: To admit that a joke, punchline, etc., was funny.
ex: Sutho took a pull at his Johnny Walker and Coke and laughed that trademark laugh of his and said: `Okay. I'll pay that all right.'

senses.d: Money given in return for work; salary or wages.
ex: Many employers have rules designed to keep employees from comparing their pays.

senses.d: A paying job; a paying concern.
Operable or accessible on deposit of coins.
ex: pay toilet

senses.d: Pertaining to or requiring payment.
ex: pay television

senses.d: To cover (the bottom of a vessel, a seam, a spar, etc.) with tar or pitch, or a waterproof composition of tallow, resin, etc.; to smear.
